abstract:
Single-cell multi-omics sequencing enables joint profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility, yet high-quality paired data remain scarce. Cross-modal translation based on generative modeling enables inference of an unmeasured modality from limited paired observations. However, substantial differences between gene expression and chromatin accessibility complicate cross-modal relationship modeling and the effective use of observed-modality information to guide target-modality generation.
We propose scPriorDiff, a biological network prior-guided conditional latent diffusion model. scPriorDiff integrates diverse biological networks into a multimodal heterogeneous graph and employs a message-passing graph neural network (GNN) to learn biologically informed modality-specific representations that capture cross-modal and intra-modal relationships. To enable full-graph representation learning, a prior-regularized cross-modal completion module infers target-modality node representations during inference. The GNN-derived source representation conditions diffusion for target-modality generation. Across six paired single-cell multi-omics datasets, scPriorDiff outperformed eight representative methods and showed strong generalization across batches and to unseen cell types. Downstream analyses further demonstrated that the generated profiles preserved cell identities, molecular signatures, and biologically relevant functions.
The scPriorDiff software is publicly available at https://github.com/ChrisOliver2345/scPriorDiff and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23408383.
Supplementary data are available as a separate file.
